title: Callback hell and composing async before Promises
hook: Nested fs.readFile callbacks formed pyramid-shaped code that was hard to read, hard to error-handle, and hard to parallelize. Named functions, modular steps, and promisify were the bridge before async/await.

blocks.text: **Callback hell** (pyramid of doom) is deep nesting when each async step starts inside the previous callback. Causes: sequential async with callback API, inline anonymous functions, and mixed error handling. **Mitigations before Promises**: split **named functions**, **async.waterfall** (async.js), **promisify** + **Promise.all**, and **generator + co**. Modern code uses **async/await**, but interviews still ask you to refactor nested callbacks.

entries.plainDefinition: Rightward indentation from nested callbacks — readability and maintenance cost.
entries.example: Three levels of fs.readFile each inside the previous callback.

entries.plainDefinition: Pass next step as callback instead of returning — all Node callbacks are CPS.
Run async tasks sequentially passing result to next — async.js pattern.
Convert error-first callback API to Promise-returning function.
entries.example: const steps = [readA, readB].map(f => promisify(f)); await pipeline(steps);

blocks.text: Legacy codebases still contain nested callbacks. Understanding composition teaches **why** Promises and async/await won — shared error channel, linear reading order, and Promise.all for parallel steps. C# never had callback hell at scale because Task/async arrived early; JS history makes this a cultural interview topic.

blocks.title: Interview trap: parallel vs sequential
blocks.body: Nested callbacks imply sequential execution. If steps are independent, nested structure is wrong — use parallel Promise.all, not deeper nesting.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Extract named functions
items.body: Each step becomes function (err, data) => next(err, transform(data)).

items.title: Centralize error handling
items.body: Single if (err) return done(err) per step or wrapper.

items.title: Promisify each step
items.body: await step1(); await step2(); linear like sync code.

snippet.label: Failure mode: swallowing errors in nested cb
snippet.explanation: Must propagate err to outer cb or reject Promise — silent log leaves caller waiting forever.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Nesting when steps are independent. Forgetting to return after err check — fall-through executes success path. Mixing callback and Promise in same function without documenting dual API.

blocks.text: Migration strategy: promisify leaf APIs, convert bottom-up, add integration tests at each layer. For remaining callback libs, use **Promise** constructor wrapper at boundary only — do not promisify mid-stack twice. Understand **unhandled rejection** replaced unhandled callback errors — still need global handlers.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Cannot refactor three-level nest to async/await. Nesting independent fetches instead of Promise.all. Not propagating errors to caller.

interviewTakeaways: Callback hell = nested CPS — duplicated err handling and poor parallelism.
Fix: named functions, promisify, async/await, Promise.all for independent steps.
Always propagate errors — log alone leaves callers hanging.
60s: Pyramid from nested err-first callbacks. Refactor with promisify and await. Parallel with Promise.all not nesting. C# had Task early; JS evolved through Promises.
Follow-up: refactor waterfall where step2 needs step1 output but step3 is independent.
commonPitfalls: Sequential nesting when operations could run in parallel.
Logging err without calling outer callback or rejecting Promise.
Strong answer: show before/after refactor, Promise.all, single try/catch, C# contrast.

jsTsCorrelations.note: async function always returns Promise — TypeScript helps enforce await only on Promise-like values during migration from callbacks.
Promise libraries bridged callback era to native Promise — historical context for why composition improved.
